title: Local Kubernetes with kind and k3d: start here
description: What this learning lab covers, in which order to read it, and the one rule to follow before you run anything.

toc.text: The whole thing on one page

html:
How to run a real, multi-node Kubernetes cluster on your own computer, using kind or k3d (Kubernetes in Docker), then deploy apps into it, one at a time, into namespaces you choose. It is a learning lab: cheap to build, safe to break, gone in one command.

Written from a working setup on macOS (Apple Silicon, Docker Desktop, Homebrew). The idea is general: only the install commands are macOS-specific.

#Read in this order

FileWhat it gives you
Concepts: what each piece isThe words and ideas: kind, nodes, taints, contexts and kubeconfig, namespaces (including kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease), pods, Services. Read once, come back as needed.
Users and permissions: who may do what, in which namespaceWho may do what in which namespace: RBAC (Roles, bindings, ServiceAccounts), hands-on users and groups, and the layers of a complete cluster ACL.
Create a local Kubernetes cluster with kindInstall the tools, create the 3-node cluster local-cluster-1 with kind, switch to it, look at the nodes, make namespaces.
Create a local Kubernetes cluster with k3dThe same with k3d, plus what k3d adds: live node add/remove, load balancer, ingress, metrics, a built-in registry, a dashboard.
Run your own image in the clusterGet an image you built into the cluster and run it: kind load, or a local registry.
Deploy apps into your namespaces, one at a timeDeploy apps into the namespaces one at a time, place pods on nodes, and use them: port-forward, DNS between namespaces, NodePort, scaling.
Deploy with a Helm 2 chart: every template, explainedPackage an app as a Helm 2 chart and deploy it: every template explained (Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, image pull secret regsecret, Ingress, autoscaling, hooks and more), plus Tiller setup and a production checklist.
Stop, shut down and clean upDelete the namespaces, stop and start the cluster, or shut everything down and remove the kubectl context.

#Try it in your browser

Every command in these guides can be run first in the KubeDojo playground: a simulator of kind, k3d, docker, kubectl and Helm 2 with a live picture of the cluster. Nothing touches your computer, so you can follow along, make mistakes and reset. When it works, the playground can export the same cluster as a setup script for your real machine.

Open the playground

Start with 01 (kind) or 02 (k3d). After that 03 and 04 work on either, in any order.

#The whole thing on one page

What the kind guide builds, with the commands it uses:

StepWhat happensThe command
1Install the toolsbrew install kind kubectl
2Describe a 3-node cluster named local-cluster-1write kind-config.yaml
3Create it (runs Docker containers as nodes)kind create cluster --config kind-config.yaml
4Point kubectl at itkubectl config use-context kind-local-cluster-1
5Check the nodeskubectl get nodes
6Label the workers to place pods laterkubectl label node <node> role=<value>
7Make namespaceskubectl create namespace <name>
8Deploy an app into a namespacekubectl create deployment <name> --image=<image> -n <namespace>
9Give it a stable namekubectl expose deployment <name> --port=<port> -n <namespace>
10Look at it, from your local machinekubectl get pods -A -o wide, kubectl port-forward
11Remove itkind delete cluster --name local-cluster-1

Time: about 15 minutes the first run (most of it downloading images), a couple of minutes after that.

#What you need

  • A Mac (or Linux) with Docker running, and about 4–8 GB of memory given to it.
  • Homebrew for the install commands.
  • A terminal. Everything is typed commands; no GUI steps except Docker's settings.

#One rule before you start

kubectl sends every command to the current context. If your computer also has a cloud or work cluster in ~/.kube/config, that cluster may be the current one. Before any command that changes something:

It should say kind-local-cluster-1 (or k3d-local-cluster-1).
